summary: Ninety-odd compliance statements, the great majority Rust and TUI style guidance, with six genuinely mechanical ordering rules buried in them. Contains the corpus's best polarity traps: an instruction to install dependencies, an instruction not to ask for approval, and a 'No history rewrite' rule about model context rather than git.

policies.quote: When using format! and you can inline variables into {}, always do that.
Install any commands the repo relies on (for example `just`, `rg`, or `cargo-insta`) if they aren't already available before running instructions here.
policies.note: An instruction TO install, in a corpus where every other dependency rule forbids it. A reader keyed on the words install and dependency gets the polarity backwards and reports a no-install rule the document contradicts.

policies.quote: Never add or modify any code related to `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` or `CODEX_SANDBOX_ENV_VAR`.
policies.note: Scope expressed as two symbol names rather than two paths, which is the part a path-shaped target extractor drops.

policies.quote: Always collapse if statements
Always inline format! args when possible
Use method references over closures when possible
Avoid bool or ambiguous `Option` parameters that force callers to write hard-to-read code
Use an exact `/*param_name*/` comment before opaque literal arguments
Do not add these comments for string or char literals unless the comment adds real clarity
The parameter name in the comment must exactly match the callee signature.
When possible, make `match` statements exhaustive and avoid wildcard arms.
Newly added traits should include doc comments that explain their role
Discourage both `#[async_trait]` and `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` in Rust traits.
Do not use `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` as a shortcut
When writing tests, prefer comparing the equality of entire objects over fields one by one.
Do not add tests for values that are statically defined.
policies.note: A rule about not writing certain tests. Reading it as protect-tests inverts it.

policies.quote: Do not add negative tests for logic that was removed.
Do not add general product or user-facing documentation to the `docs/` folder.
policies.note: A path-shaped scope rule with a stated exception in the next sentence.

policies.quote: Prefer private modules and explicitly exported public crate API.
If you change `ConfigToml` or nested config types, run `just write-config-schema` to update `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json`.
prefer using `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/mcp_connection_manager.rs` to handle mutation of tools and tool calls
Do not call `reset_client_session` unnecessarily

If you change Rust dependencies (`Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`), run `just bazel-lock-update` from the
  repo root to refresh `MODULE.bazel.lock`, and include that lockfile update in the same change.
policies.note: Names its own enforcement in the next sentence: CI verifies lockfile drift.

policies.quote: update the crate's `BUILD.bazel`
Do not create small helper methods that are referenced only once.

instrument the function or method definition with
  `#[tracing::instrument(...)]` instead of attaching spans to futures
Prefer adding new modules instead of growing existing ones.
Target Rust modules under 500 LoC, excluding tests.
If a file exceeds roughly 800 LoC, add new functionality in a new module

Avoid adding new standalone methods to `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs` unless the change is
    trivial
be patient with the command and never try to kill them using the PID
policies.note: Forbids killing a process, which is the shape of a destructive-command rule and is not one.

policies.quote: Run `just fmt` (in the `codex-rs` directory) automatically after you have finished making code changes anywhere in this repository; do not ask for approval to run it.
policies.note: Contains an explicit anti-ask-first clause. A reader keyed on the word approval files this as ask-first, which is the opposite of what it says.

policies.quote: Do not run `cargo test` directly. Use `just test` so test execution follows the repo defaults.
Run the test for the specific project that was changed.
project-specific or individual tests can be run without asking the user, but do ask the user before running the complete test suite.
policies.note: A conditional ask-first: the same command is free at one scope and gated at another. Extracted without the condition it becomes either a blanket prohibition or nothing.

policies.quote: Before finalizing a large change to `codex-rs`, run `just fix -p <project>`
Do not re-run tests after running `fix` or `fmt`.
**resist adding code to codex-core**!
do not hesitate to push back on PRs that would unnecessarily add code to `codex-core`
Keep crate API surfaces as small as possible. Avoid proliferating test-only helpers.
No history rewrite - the context must be built up incrementally.
policies.note: 'History rewrite' here is the model's message context, not git history. The strongest no-force-push false friend in the corpus.

policies.quote: No unbounded items - everything injected in the model context must have a bounded size and a hard cap.
No items larger than 10K tokens.
All injected fragments must be defined as structs in `core/context` and implement ContextualUserFragment trait
Search for breaking changes in external integration surfaces:
For agent changes prefer integration tests over unit tests.
Features that change the agent logic MUST add an integration test:
policies.note: About adding tests, not protecting them.

policies.quote: If unit tests are needed, put them in a dedicated test file
Avoid test-only functions in the main implementation.
the total number of changed lines should not exceed 800 lines
For complex logic changes the size should be under 500 lines.
Use concise styling helpers from ratatui’s Stylize trait.
Prefer Stylize helpers
Avoid hardcoded white: do not use `.white()`; prefer the default foreground (no color).
Chaining: combine helpers by chaining for readability
Single items: prefer "text".into()
Building lines: use vec![…].into() to construct a Line when the target type is obvious
Avoid churn: don’t refactor between equivalent forms
Compactness: prefer the form that stays on one line after rustfmt
Always use textwrap::wrap to wrap plain strings.
use the helpers in tui/src/wrapping.rs
use the initial_indent / subsequent_indent options from RtOptions
use the `prefix_lines` helper from line_utils
When adding a new test module, define its contents in a separate sibling file rather than inline in the implementation file.
Use an explicit `#[path = "..._tests.rs"]` attribute
Do not move or rewrite existing inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` modules solely to follow this convention.
policies.note: A rule protecting existing test modules from rewriting. The nearest thing here to protect-tests, and it is about layout, not assertions.

policies.quote:
any change that affects user-visible UI (including adding new UI) must include
corresponding `insta` snapshot coverage
Only if you intend to accept all new snapshots in this crate, run:
Tests should use pretty_assertions::assert_eq for clearer diffs.
Prefer deep equals comparisons whenever possible.
Avoid mutating process environment in tests; prefer passing environment-derived flags or dependencies from above.
Prefer `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin("...")` over `assert_cmd::Command::cargo_bin(...)`
avoid `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`
Prefer the utilities in `core_test_support::responses` when writing end-to-end Codex tests.
Use `TestCodexBuilder::build_with_auto_env()` by default
hold onto it so you can assert against outbound `/responses` POST bodies
Prefer `wait_for_event` over `wait_for_event_with_timeout`.
Prefer `mount_sse_once` over `mount_sse_once_match` or `mount_sse_sequence`
Tests should exercise app-server's public JSON-RPC API.
All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.
Follow payload naming consistently:
Expose RPC methods as `<resource>/<method>` and keep `<resource>` singular
Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
Always set `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` on v2 request/response/notification types
Never use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for v2 API payload fields.
Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned.
Prefer plain `String` IDs at the API boundary
Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (`i64`) and named `*_at`
Every optional field must be annotated with `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`.
For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default:

Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change:
  `just write-app-server-schema`
Validate with `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol`.
Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers
You should not use the `__future__` module.
Tests and features must support Linux, macOS and Windows unless feature is explicitly OS-specific.
if any changes were made in common, core, or protocol, run the complete test suite with `just test`
policies.note: Added after a run extracted it; the annotation had covered only the sentence after it.

policies.quote: Avoid `--all-features` for routine local runs
Prefer scoping with `-p` to avoid slow workspace‑wide Clippy builds

traps.quote: `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1` will be set whenever you use the `shell` tool
traps.why: Describes the sandbox the agent already runs in. Treating it as a control this repository enforces would be a false GATE about something outside the repository.

traps.quote: cargo benchmarks can be run with `just bench`

traps.why: An install command offered as help. The second place in this document where install text is not a dependency policy.

traps.quote: Codex maintains a context (history of messages) that is sent to the model in inference requests.
traps.why: Architecture description, and the sentence that makes 'No history rewrite' two lines later mean message context rather than git history.
